Date: 2024-05-15
Provider: Dr. Aisha Patel, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Acute right arm swelling and heaviness after intensive weight training

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient with familial hypercholesterolemia, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy, and athletic heart syndrome presents with right arm swelling. He is a personal trainer recently beginning a new regimen including intensive weight lifting and repetitive overhead arm exercises.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Familial Hypercholesterolemia (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- First-degree atrioventricular block with Mobitz type I second-degree AV block (Athletic heart syndrome) (diagnosed 2020-03-15)
- Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (diagnosed 2020-07-15)
- Chronic anal fissure (diagnosed 2022-07-15)
- Pilonidal abscess (diagnosed 2023-03-15)
- Musculoskeletal chest pain (diagnosed 2023-10-15)
- Familial hypercholesterolemia (heterozygous)
- Athletic heart syndrome with AV conduction abnormalities (first-degree AV block and Wenckebach)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Atorvastatin 80 mg PO daily
- Metoprolol succinate 50 mg PO daily

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with ICD placement
- Mother: Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia, premature coronary artery disease (MI at age 45)
- Paternal uncle: Sudden cardiac death at age 28

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Software Developer and Part-time Personal Trainer.

VITAL SIGNS:
His vital signs are stable, and the rest of the physical examination is unremarkable.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, his right arm is visibly swollen compared to the left, with pitting edema and tenderness along the course of the deep veins. There is no erythema or warmth.

LABORATORY DATA:
His complete blood count, coagulation profile, and basic metabolic panel are within normal limits.

IMAGING:
An ultrasound of the right upper extremity shows noncompressible segments in the axillary and subclavian veins.

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Several weeks of sharp rectal pain during bowel movements

He describes the pain as sharp and cutting, occurring specifically during bowel movements and followed by a dull ache that lingers for a few hours. He has noticed himself holding in stool to avoid the pain, which has made him more constipated over time. He delayed seeking care due to embarrassment but states the pain has now started to interfere with his ability to work.

- Familial hypercholesterolemia (heterozygous)
- Athletic heart syndrome with AV conduction abnormalities (first-degree AV block and Wenckebach)

He reports no personal or family history of gastrointestinal conditions. He is otherwise healthy.

MEDICATIONS:
He does not take any medications.

Home Medications:
- Atorvastatin 80 mg PO daily
- Metoprolol succinate 50 mg PO daily

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
He reports no personal or family history of gastrointestinal conditions.

SOCIAL HISTORY:
His job involves sitting for most of the day.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2023-03-15
Provider: Dr. Aisha Patel, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Worsening lower back pain with fever and purulent drainage

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient with familial hypercholesterolemia, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy, and prior rectal pain presents with lower back pain. He reports pain intensifies with prolonged sitting, occasional fevers, and foul-smelling discharge from the same area.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Familial Hypercholesterolemia (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- First-degree atrioventricular block with Mobitz type I second-degree AV block (Athletic heart syndrome) (diagnosed 2020-03-15)
- Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (diagnosed 2020-07-15)
- Chronic anal fissure (diagnosed 2022-07-15)
- Familial hypercholesterolemia (heterozygous)
- Athletic heart syndrome with AV conduction abnormalities (first-degree AV block and Wenckebach)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Atorvastatin 80 mg PO daily
- Metoprolol succinate 50 mg PO daily

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with ICD placement
- Mother: Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia, premature coronary artery disease (MI at age 45)
- Paternal uncle: Sudden cardiac death at age 28

SOCIAL HISTORY:
He works as a software developer, often spending long hours seated

VITAL SIGNS:
His vital signs are as follows:

- Temperature: 38.2°C (100.8°F)
- Blood pressure: 125/78 mmHg
- Heart rate: 88 beats per minute
- Respiratory rate: 16 breaths per minute

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, there is a tender, fluctuant mass located approximately 4 cm cephalad to the anus in the midline of the intergluteal cleft. There is erythema and purulent drainage noted around the mass.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2021-03-15
Provider: Dr. Maria Rodriguez, MD
Department: Sports Medicine
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Pre-participation health examination for marathon training

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
He returns for cardiac follow-up. He has no complaints and is currently training for an upcoming international marathon.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Familial Hypercholesterolemia (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- First-degree atrioventricular block with Mobitz type I second-degree AV block (Athletic heart syndrome) (diagnosed 2020-03-15)
- Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (diagnosed 2020-07-15)
- Familial hypercholesterolemia (heterozygous)
- Athletic heart syndrome with AV conduction abnormalities (first-degree AV block and Wenckebach)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Atorvastatin 80 mg PO daily
- Metoprolol succinate 50 mg PO daily

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
His family history is negative for cardiac disease.

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Software Developer and Part-time Personal Trainer.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:
He denies any history of syncope, dizziness, chest pain, or palpitations.

VITAL SIGNS:
On examination, his blood pressure is 110/70 mmHg, heart rate is 48 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 14 beats per minute.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
His physical examination is otherwise unremarkable.

LABORATORY DATA:
His laboratory values are as follows:

- Hemoglobin: 14.5 g/dL
- Hematocrit: 42%
- Sodium: 140 mEq/L
- Potassium: 4.2 mEq/L
- Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL
- Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH): 2.5 μIU/mL

OTHER STUDIES:
An electrocardiogram (ECG) is performed, which shows a regular rhythm with a prolonged PR interval of 220 ms and occasional dropped beats that are not preceded by a progressive PR interval prolongation.
